items.root_cause: the re-arm is per key and every key carries its own clock, so a standing backlog of reviewed-but-unfixable flags pages on a different day almost every day. Nothing about any single one of those mails is wrong, which is why seven fixes to individual flags never moved the type: the class cannot go quiet while the backlog stands, because the backlog itself is the emitter's schedule. Fixing the flags one at a time cannot reach it and neither can any exclude

root_fix.what: coalesce at the emitter: a re-arm rides a page day, it never opens one. Genuinely new events (a key never seen, one that cleared and came back, an ack that ran out, a key with no usable clock) are untouched and still page same-day
root_fix.exact_change: as surface_fix, plus four frozen cases in test-auditors unit u067 that drive the REAL extracted REVIEW-DECISION and REVIEW-STAMP regions against a frozen two-key backlog

all eight are lane state or lane ledgers of the same class as meal-prep/db/source-domains.json and graph/identity, which bot-paths already owns for exactly the reason given in its header: an observation that never leaves this box is an observation lost

surface_fix.what: bot-paths.ps1 owns the eight paths the three lanes already declare
surface_fix.exact_change: Get-BotInputPaths gains grocery/notify-known-ids.json, grocery/sale-fallback-ownership.json, meal-prep/db/costed.stamp.json, meal-prep/db/candidate-pool.json, meal-prep/db/harvest-state.json, meal-prep/db/considered-dishes.json, graph/learning and graph/state, with the measurement and the reason in the comment above them

items.root_cause: two declarations of one fact, written separately: lib/pipeline-commit.ps1 Get-PipelinePaths says what each lane owns and lib/bot-paths.ps1 says what an automated commit may touch. Nothing compared them, so they drifted apart and the pre-commit hook refused each lane's OWN commit the first day one of its undeclared paths was dirty

root_fix.what: the self-test compares the two declarations directly, so the next path added to either one cannot silently disagree
root_fix.exact_change: lib/bot-paths.ps1 -SelfTest dot-sources lib/pipeline-commit.ps1 and asserts, per lane, that every path Get-PipelinePaths declares is owned, naming the offenders rather than counting them

blast_radius.measured_by: Test-BotPathOwned over all three Get-PipelinePaths lists before and after the edit, plus lib/bot-paths.ps1 -SelfTest
blast_radius.risk: this WIDENS what an automated commit may stage, which is the direction that cost this estate 3c44d0c1. Contained three ways: every one of the eight is already declared by a scheduled lane in the other file, so nothing new is staged that a committer was not already trying to stage; none is source, and the MUST FIRE cases for a .ps1, a design doc and a prefix sibling all still pass; and the newly owned graph paths are the exact reason the graph lane's missing start snapshot was fixed in the same plan, so a session's file dirty before the run is held back rather than swept

proof.clean_twin: the four pre-existing MUST FIRE cases still refuse a .ps1, a design doc, a prefix sibling and an empty ownership set, and a new twin asserts that a data file no lane declares is still NOT owned, so the widening did not become a sweep

items.root_cause: the foreign-held rule can only work if the CALLER hands it a snapshot taken before the run wrote anything, and nothing checked that the callers do. The rule's own fixtures all build their snapshot by hand, so a lane that passes none is invisible to them

items.subject: Triage residual: a day with no sign-in until after a task's catch-up window is still lost, and nothing reports it the next day
evidence: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-11: the residual's second half is FALSE as written. grocery/health-heartbeat.ps1 reads grocery/expected-automations.json and checks that each registered Windows task EXISTS, is not disabled, and RAN within max_age_hours, alerting through Send-Alert when it did not. All six one-shot tasks the item names are registered there: TC Grocery Ad Pulls 0700, TC Grocery Daily Capture 0800, TC Grocery Capture Watchdog 1030, TC Recall Sleep 0435, TC Brain Digest 0645 and TC Recipe Harvest Crawl, every one at max_age_hours=30 (9 tasks registered in total, 8 at 30 hours and the sidecar watchdog at 2)
so a day a task loses entirely IS reported the next day, inside 30 hours, by an existing check that pages on the FIRST occurrence

the first half stands at zero: the item measured 0 occurrences in the 20 days that have run logs (2026-08-22 to 2026-09-10, a log for every day), and the one measured gap (restart 20:33, sign-in 03:29) is covered by every task's catch-up window
the Interactive logon type is deliberate and not a defect: a non-interactive token cannot open the DPAPI-protected browser profiles (graph/pipeline/install-nightly-task.ps1:62)
items.root_cause: the residual was written from the task scheduler's side, where StartWhenAvailable does not re-queue a missed Interactive occurrence, and it did not account for health-heartbeat watching the same tasks from the artefact side. The remaining exposure is a restart plus no sign-in for a whole 4 to 8 hour window, which has not happened in 20 days of logs
items.root_fix_none_because: there is nothing to fix: the reporting half is already owned by health-heartbeat, which pages on the first occurrence, and the losing half has happened 0 times in 20 measured days behind a logon type that is required for the work

blast_radius.measured_by: read of grocery/expected-automations.json (9 registered tasks with their max_age_hours) and of health-heartbeat.ps1's task check and Send-Alert path

items.freshness: measured 2026-09-11 against expected-automations.json and health-heartbeat.ps1 at HEAD. If a task is ever added to Task Scheduler and not to that registry, health-heartbeat's own TASK UNWATCHED issue is what says so

proof.guard_or_fixture: grocery/health-heartbeat.ps1, already scheduled and already alerting
proof.must_fire_case: a registered task that has not run within max_age_hours (30) is reported as a silent death and mailed
proof.clean_twin: a task registered in Task Scheduler but absent from expected-automations.json is reported as TASK UNWATCHED rather than passing quietly

items.resolution_note: Closed by-design after re-measurement. The reporting half of the residual is false as written: health-heartbeat.ps1 checks all six one-shot tasks through expected-automations.json at max_age_hours=30 and mails on the first occurrence, so a lost day IS reported the next day. The losing half has happened 0 times in the 20 days that have run logs, the one measured gap is covered by the catch-up windows shipped 2026-09-10, and the Interactive logon type is required for the DPAPI-protected browser profiles. Residual owned by watch:grocery/health-heartbeat.ps1 at 0 occurrences.
items.premise_verified: false, and that is the finding: the premise 'nothing reports it the next day' does not hold. The six tasks are registered in expected-automations.json at 30 hours and health-heartbeat mails on the first miss
items.deviation: closed rather than fixed, because the measurement removed the work
items.leaves_open: a restart followed by no sign-in for a whole catch-up window still loses that task's day; the loss is reported, not prevented

items.subject: Triage residual: a session edit made during a pipeline run is still swept into that run's commit
evidence: the class is real and structural: both committers stage by DIRECTORY (grocery/out alone is 1,342 tracked files) and the foreign-held rule shipped on 2026-09-10 discriminates by MTIME against the run start, so a file a session edits AFTER the run started has a newer mtime and is indistinguishable from one the run wrote

re-measured only as far as the budget allowed: the rule is in lib/pipeline-commit.ps1 as Get-ForeignHeldPaths and its input is a mtime map, so no version of it can see this case. No occurrence count was taken over the last 14 days of bot commits; that measurement is the first thing the next lane should buy

this plan's 47eafb fix widens the exposure slightly, by giving the three lanes ownership of 8 paths the scope hook used to refuse on their behalf (graph/learning, graph/state and six ledgers). The pre-run half of those is covered by the foreign-held rule and, for the graph lane, by the start snapshot shipped here under a86b87
items.root_cause: ownership is inferred from mtime, and mtime cannot distinguish an author. A rule that could would have to compare content against what the run itself wrote (a per-file write journal kept by the run) rather than when the file changed
items.root_fix_none_because: not attempted: the item ceiling went on the four items above it. Nothing was shipped and nothing was weakened

blast_radius.risk: unchanged: nothing shipped for this item

items.freshness: not re-measured beyond reading the rule at HEAD 359d7c3c7 on 2026-09-11

proof.must_fire_case: for whoever picks it up: a file CLEAN at run start, edited by a session mid-run, must not be staged by the run's commit
proof.clean_twin: a file the run itself wrote mid-run must still be committed as the run's own

do_not_touch: the mtime rule that shipped on 2026-09-10, which is correct for the pre-run case
items.resolution_note: NOT WORKED: the lane's item budget ran out above it. The class was re-read and stands (ownership is inferred from mtime, which cannot see an edit made after the run started, so a write journal kept by the run is the shape of any real fix). No occurrence count was taken and nothing shipped; the id stays open and un-minted.
items.premise_verified: partially: the mtime rule was re-read at HEAD and cannot see this case. The occurrence count over recent bot commits was NOT taken
items.leaves_open: the whole class: a session edit made during a run is still swept into that run's commit
items.leaves_open_window: not measured this run, which is itself the first thing the next lane should buy

items.subject: Triage finding: source-domains -Record lost 1 of 8 concurrent writes and refused a push
evidence: already closed before this lane reached it: triage-queue.json has 2026-09-10-c069fa at status=resolved, resolved_ts 2026-09-11T14:41:51, disposition=confirmed

its close names the cause and the fix: Move-Item -Force over the ledger threw 'Cannot create a file when that file already exists' whenever another process held the file open without FileShare.Delete, measured at 3 of 40 self-test runs on unchanged code; fixed by 9f3ca3cbd (lib/atomic-write.ps1 retry), and main at 7107ce79e passed the self-test 80 of 80
items.root_cause: see the close: the write step inside the mutex, not the lock and not the barrier
items.root_fix_none_because: already shipped by another lane at 9f3ca3cbd; there is nothing for this lane to do

blast_radius.measured_by: not re-measured: the item is closed and its close carries the measurement

proof.guard_or_fixture: meal-prep/pipeline/source-domains.ps1 -SelfTest concurrency case, kept and not weakened

items.resolution_note: Superseded: closed as confirmed at 14:41 on 2026-09-11 by the lane that shipped 9f3ca3cbd, before this weekly lane reached it. Nothing done here. Its own follow-up (drop the unused pre-lock read) is recorded in that close and is not minted as a new id.
items.premise_verified: true: the queue says resolved, and the close names the commit
